answer.short: Domain $[-2,0]$; range $[0,\pi]$. Translate $y=\sin^{-1}x$ left 1 unit and up $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

$$\begin{align*}-1&\le x+1\le1\\-2&\le x\le0.\end{align*}$$
For the range,
$$\begin{align*}-\frac\pi2&\le\sin^{-1}(x+1)\le\frac\pi2\\0&\le y\le\pi.\end{align*}$$
Translate the standard inverse-sine graph left 1 unit and up $\frac{\pi}{2}$. Draw the increasing curve through $(-2,0)$, $(-1,\frac{\pi}{2})$ and $(0,\pi)$.

answer.short: Domain $\mathbb R$; range $(-\pi,0)$. Translate $y=\tan^{-1}x$ down $\frac{\pi}{2}$; asymptotes $y=-\pi$ and $y=0$.
answer.worked:
The domain remains $\mathbb R$.
$$\begin{align*}-\frac\pi2&<\tan^{-1}x<\frac\pi2\\-\pi&<y<0.\end{align*}$$
Translate the standard inverse-tangent graph down $\frac{\pi}{2}$. The increasing curve passes through $(0,-\frac{\pi}{2})$ and approaches $y=-\pi$ on the left and $y=0$ on the right.
